# R116 — K1 native light and compact controls

Build V20.6-R11.6-K1-LIGHT-2026-10-17, stable sequence116, version1.14.5, based on published R115.

On stock K1 firmware without a discoverable Klipper light output, Farm reads the separate Creality LAN WebSocket on the same authorized printer IP, fixed port9999 and path/. Support is enabled only after a numeric binary lightSw state is actually received. It sends only the fixed lightSw0/1 set frames. Generic G-code, print control, temperatures, fan commands and arbitrary native payloads are not exposed by this command.

The wire contract was checked directly in CrealityOfficial/CrealityPrint commit59ae8cbb0437dcc7236e27433ecd4aeb52be0244, resources/web/deviceMgr/assets/BZCDzYbb.js (DeviceInterface.SetSwitchState and lightSw state merger). Initial status is unsolicited; ReqPrinterPara1 is a compatibility refresh used by maintained LAN integrations.

Native control first observes a current state on a new connection, drains prewrite telemetry, sends the set frame once and waits for a later matching lightSw state. A socket write, heartbeat or acknowledgement never counts as state confirmation. Read/write/handshake are bounded to six seconds; input is limited to64KiB. No automatic write retry or guessed SET_PIN PIN=LED fallback remains. Existing discovered Klipper pin/LED/macro targets retain their command path, with a read-only exact-object GET fallback for missing RPC state.

Read-only light status requires a Viewer session; setting light requires Operator. The command retains saved-printer target authorization and scheduler priority and always derives the fixed LAN socket from the authorized resolved printer address. No new dependency or credential is added.

The utility area uses three compact ranges for speed, fan and light. Unknown light state has a neutral position; left is off and right is on. A requested value is not presented as confirmed. Login, print/upload, discovery, camera guard, TV and update behavior are retained from R115; check-creality-light.mjs enforces the protected source regions.

Validation:11 production client behavior cases;10 actual Rust light wire/parser/deadline tests; Windows UI acceptance covers13 light scenarios,12 full-panel layouts and existing29 auth cases. Physical K1 Max is not available in the build environment. Windows installer and R115→R116 upgrade must pass before publication.
